title: ‘Shoulder-fired missile’ threat: Why Trump was made to secretly switch planes after Nato summit in Turkey
content:
• US President Donald Trump secretly switched from Air Force One to a smaller C-32A jet on July 8, after the NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, due due to a credible 'shoulder-fired missile' threat.
• The Secret Service orchestrated the security deception, transferring President Trump via a catering truck, while the older Air Force One departed separately as a decoy carrying officials including Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
• The extraordinary security measure was prompted by US intelligence indicating Iran possessed precise information about Trump's location in Ankara and reports of an individual with a shoulder-fired missile near the NATO summit.

title: Tehran signals shift to ‘offensive’ military doctrine, rules out extension of June interim deal
content:
• Mohammad Reza Naqdi, an adviser to the commander of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), stated that Tehran is moving toward an “offensive doctrine.”
• An interim agreement reached in June provided a 60-day period for negotiations, but Iran has rejected its extension, citing alleged US violations.
• The strategically vital Strait of Hormuz, which handled about one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas flows before the conflict, is a major point of contention, with Iran threatening its closure.

title: Trump says Iran has ‘No Money’, blasts Tehran over ‘300% INFLATION’ as he touts ‘WALL OF STEEL’ naval blockade in Strait
content:

• The Strait of Hormuz is a crucial global energy corridor linking the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman.
• Tehran is seeking compensation for losses attributed to sanctions and a conflict launched by Donald Trump on February 28.

title: Only 65% get jobs, 6 lakh youth remain unplaced; panel flags rural jobs scheme’s placement gap
content:
• The Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) has trained 18.38 lakh rural youth but placed 11.94 lakh, achieving an overall placement ratio of 65% against its 70% target.
• DDU-GKY 2.0 guidelines, effective from April 1, 2025, will increase the minimum placement period from three to six months and allow for self-employment and gig employment while retaining the 70% overall placement requirement.
• An independent evaluation of DDU-GKY (April 2016 to December 2023) found an average monthly salary of around ₹16,500 for placed trainees, with 86.73% of placements aligned with their trades.

title: Air India Phuket-Delhi pilot had sleep issues, was on medication before flight: Report
content:
• On 4 August, Air India flight AI2379 (Airbus A320neo) from Phuket to Delhi lost approximately 300 feet in altitude while carrying 137 passengers, 6 cabin crew, and 2 pilots.
• The pilot-in-command of Air India flight AI2379 tested positive for marijuana in a confirmatory drug screening after the incident.
• The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) is investigating the incident, which was referred after being classified as a serious incident, with the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) determining regulatory action.

title: Iran had detailed intel on Trump’s Ankara stay, including his floor: Report
content:
• US President Donald Trump secretly switched aircraft in Ankara, Turkey, on July 8 during the NATO summit following a credible security threat.
• The threat, identified by US officials, originated from Iranian intelligence and involved a potential surface-to-air missile targeting Air Force One.
• Trump had used a newly renovated Boeing 747-8 aircraft, donated by Qatar, for his travel to Ankara, which marked its first international trip with him.

title: RBI proposes new interest rate rules for regulated entities, seeks public comments
content:
• The final guidelines for interest rates on regulated entity loans shall come into effect from April 1, 2027, with all existing loans required to migrate to the new framework by April 1, 2029.
• The RBI has defined small value loans as personal loans where the principal amount does not exceed Rs 50,000, for which Regulated Entities (REs) must explicitly put a ceiling on the Annual Percentage Rate (APR).
• For floating rate loans, the benchmark reset period shall not exceed three months, and for agricultural loans, it shall not exceed 12 months (linked to crop season). All floating rate personal loans and loans extended to MSMEs by commercial banks shall be linked to an external benchmark.

title: Inflation likely to rise from here as food prices remain key risk: Experts
content:
• India's retail inflation rose to 4.45 per cent in July from 4.38 per cent in June, as per data from the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
• Food inflation, measured by the Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI), increased to 5.52 per cent in July from 5.32 per cent in June.
• Retail inflation is expected to remain below the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) 6 per cent upper tolerance limit.

title: India sets sail to add more trade muscle as it signs PTA terms with SACU
content:
• India has signed the Terms of Reference (ToRs) for a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) with the Southern African Customs Union (SACU), comprising South Africa, Botswana, Namibia, Lesotho, and Eswatini.
• India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal discussed the signing of ToRs for the India-SACU PTA in an August 6 post on X after meeting Parks Tau, Minister of Trade, Industry and Competition of South Africa. The agreement was officially signed by Ndiitah Nghipondoka Robiati (Namibia) and Yashvir Singh (India).
• In FY2025-26, India's exports to SACU totaled $7.5 billion, while imports stood at $9.2 billion. Bilateral trade between India and South Africa, the largest trading partner within SACU, dipped by 13.55% to $15.56 billion in FY2025-26 from $18 billion in FY2024-25.
